 Formula One 2026 São Paulo Grand Prix: Formula One 2026 – live
 🏎️ Updates from Interlagos (race due to start 5pm GMT)
 🏎️ Email Daniel | Sign up for The Recap 
 LIVE  Updated  1m ago Daniel Harris Sun 8 Nov 2026 12.31 EST First published on Sun 8 Nov 2026 11.00 EST Share Key events 1h ago The starting grid 
 2h ago Preamble 
 Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads the field into turn one at the start during the F1 Grand Prix of Brazil at Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace. Photograph: Clive Rose/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads the field into turn one at the start during the F1 Grand Prix of Brazil at Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace. Photograph: Clive Rose/Getty Images Daniel Harris Sun 8 Nov 2026 12.31 EST First published on Sun 8 Nov 2026 11.00 EST Share Key events 1h ago The starting grid 
 2h ago Preamble 
 36s ago 12.31 EST Lap 19/71 Norris, with tyres a lap warmer than Antonelli, cuts the leads to 0.483s. Can he get while the going’s good? Not thus far.
 Share Updated at  12.31 EST 2m ago 12.29 EST Lap 18/71 Now Antonelli pits but will he come out ahead of Norris? Yes he will, the lad down to two 1.1s. This is a different race now.
 Share 3m ago 12.28 EST Lap 17/71 The other teams will have noticed Hamilton’s pace there, and a slew of stops ensure, Norris, Russell, Hadjar, Lawson Piastri and Hulkenberg all go in … with Russell spinning! He almost nails his wing, but loses time, coming out 10th.
 Share 5m ago 12.26 EST Lap 16/71 In 13th, Alonso is giving Leclerc plenty, then he moves up a spot when Albon pits. Hamilton, meantime, is moving much more smoothly now, setting the fastest time for the final sector.
 Share 6m ago 12.25 EST Lap 15/71 Norris closes the gap behind Antonelli to 6.9s, then Hamilton, who’s wanted to pit for several laps, is ordered in; he goes to softs and comes out last … oh but Sainz is in there too. Bottas, by the way, is out of the race.
 Share 8m ago 12.24 EST Lap 14/71 We’re getting towards the first round of stops; will anyone try slicks from here until the end? There’s a fair bit of shpritz kicking up, but the lack of grip might be a problem.
 Share 9m ago 12.23 EST Lap 13/71 The top seven are well clear now, Hulkenberg 7.3s behind Piastri in seventh. Antonelli now leads Norris by 8.2s.
 Share 10m ago 12.22 EST Lap 12/71 Antonelli has stepped on it, now 8.0s in front of Norris – he’s been serene away from the drama. Russell is third, Hadjar fourth, Verstappen fifth; I quite fancy him for a podium here, he’s attacking this race like a madman.
 View image in fullscreen Kimi Antonelli leads Lando Norris and Liam Lawson of New Zealand of Racing Bulls Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images Share Updated at  12.24 EST 12m ago 12.20 EST Lap 11/71 Hadjar looked up for this from the start and he blitzes Lawson down the inside, moving into fourth; Verstappen goes past too.
 Share 13m ago 12.18 EST Lap 10/71 The two Ferraris dogfight, Hamilton on the inside, Leclerc on the right … and it’s Hamilton struggling, easily passed. His car isn’t doing what he wants, I don’t think, because that was too easy given how brilliant a driver he is.
 Share 15m ago 12.17 EST Lap 9/71 Piastri thinks Hulkenberg leaves him the inside, attacks … and past he goes. Antonelli leads by 4.7s.
 Share 16m ago 12.15 EST Lap 8/71 And now Russell passes Lawson, moving into fourth, while Versatappen passes Hulkenberg; Hamilton is told by his team to allow Bearman past, rather than face a 10-second penalty, so he does.
 Share 18m ago 12.14 EST Lap 7/71 Lawson is really struggling now and Hadjar smells it, scything by and into third place. Norris, meanwhile, takes a bit of time of Antonelli, the lead now down to 4.4s.
 Share 19m ago 12.12 EST Lap 6/71 Hamilton complains about his back tyre and is then noted for leaving the track when overtaking Bearman while, at the front, Antonelli leads by 5.3s while Lawson goes really wide, allowing Norris to get his second place back.
 View image in fullscreen Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari leads Max Verstappen in the Red Bull and Oliver Bearman in the Haas. Photograph: Mark Thompson/Getty Images Share Updated at  12.15 EST 21m ago 12.11 EST Lap 5/71 No further investigation against Verstappen, who celebrates by going around the outside of Piastri, and Albon is there for the taking too! The three are together, but it’s Verstappen with the pace and smarts, he moves up two places on one corner, and is flying now.
 Share 22m ago 12.09 EST Lap 4/71 Verstappen attacks Hamilton on the inside … and he’s far too quick, floating by and into ninth, while we learn that there’ll be no further investigation of Albon, who stays seventh.
 Share 24m ago 12.08 EST Lap 3/71 Antonelli leads by 1.2s, from Lawson, from Norris, from Hadjar, from Russell, from Hulkenberg. Meantime, Albon, seventh, is noted for being out of position at the start, so too Verstapped who’s 10th from 21st.
 Share 25m ago 12.06 EST Lap 2/71 Mercdes can win the constructors championship today if Antonelli finishes three places above the top Ferrari but he won’t care about that now – he’ll just want to see out the race. Meantime, Russell, who started seventh, is now fifth.
 Share 27m ago 12.05 EST Lap 1/71 Away we go and as we predicted, Antonelli passes Norris from the off and Hadjar also moves up past Hulkenberg, while Hamilton also progresses; oh and Liam Lawson also diddles Norris, moving into second!
 View image in fullscreen Kimi Antonelli leads at the start of the race. Photograph: Jean Carniel/Reuters Share Updated at  12.09 EST 29m ago 12.03 EST “A lot drier than I expected,” Alonso tells his team. Let’s see how things progress, because that may mean a quieter start that isn’t quite what the teams planned.
 Share 31m ago 12.01 EST Our formation lap is under way; all our drivers are on inters.
 Share Updated at  12.02 EST 32m ago 12.00 EST I’m intrigued to see how Rafael Camara goes on debut. He showed a bit of quality in qualifying, but also a fair amount of impetuousness, crashing twice and causing Leclerc agita but also making 11th on the grid. I daresay the other drivers will give him a wide berth if they can.
 Share 35m ago 11.57 EST In the list of insane achievements by youngsters, Becker winning Wimbledon at 17 is probably my pick and the one I think we’re least likely to see again. I actually think it might be the greatest sporting achievement of my lifetime, amazing though it was to see a young Tyson clobbering grown-ups. Let me know if I’m wrong…
 Share 39m ago 11.52 EST Hadjar prepares like he’s Kendall Roy going to a meeting. I think he’s got a pretty good chance of slipping by Hulkenberg at the start, but in the conditions, he’ll have to be careful.
 Share 44m ago 11.48 EST Bottas has a wheel-nut stuck. They’re trying to remove it with a hammer; if they can’t, he’ll have to use the same intermediate set all race.
 Share 45m ago 11.47 EST George Russell says yesterday was wetter but hotter. He’s not expecting conditions to dry and will be surprised to see slicks.
 Share 47m ago 11.44 EST Anthem time… 
 Share 48m ago 11.43 EST Now it’s over to Cafu, who speaks in Portuguese; “brilliant stuff,” says Brundle, no clue what he’s been told. More news as we get it.
 Share 50m ago 11.42 EST Neymar is also in attendance, but Martin Brundle can’t get a word out of him, so it’s over to Jean Alesi, who thinks Hamilton and Versatappen can get to the front. We shall see.
 Share 53m ago 11.39 EST Jesse Lingard, now or Corinthians, is at the race. “I’ve got many friends,” he says, when not asked, but is backing Red Bull having been invited on their account.
 Share 55m ago 11.37 EST Just when you think t hey’ve milked the joke to its death.
 Manchester United v Aston Villa: Premier League – live Read more Share 1h ago 11.34 EST Antonelli does, I think, have a decent short of getting by Norris at the start. His ability to pick lines, alongside the pace of the car, are pretty hard to contain.
 Share 1h ago 11.30 EST We’ve got dancers in the main straight, rain coming down. I’d not be shocked if we see some incidents today – let’s hope everyone stays safe.
 Share 1h ago 11.24 EST Oy my days! It’s raining now and Antonelli slides off the track as they go around to get into position! He’s able to adjust, but that’s a warning to all drivers.
 Share 1h ago 11.23 EST That and Pulp Fiction are the only ones I’ve seen twice in the cinema on the same day. Rightly so.
 Share 1h ago 11.23 EST On which point, if there’s been a better film this century than City of God, I’d love to know about it.
 Share 1h ago 11.22 EST Is Brazil they greatest country in the world? Well, it’s in the top one. Should you want to learn more about it, The Edge of Democracy is excellent and on Netflix, likewise Apocalypse in the Tropics . Both are directed by Petra Costa.
 Share 1h ago 11.14 EST Antonelli doesn’t – unusually for young sports stars – look older than his years. He’s all chuchi-faced and innocent, with a luxuriant head of hair, curls spilling out of his baseball cap. I am not envious, not one bit.
 Share 1h ago 11.11 EST It knows how to rain in Brazil. 
 Lando Norris claims F1 São Paulo GP pole as ‘crazy’ rain disrupts qualifying Read more It’s dry now, but it may not stay that way.
 Share 1h ago 11.09 EST Also going on:

 Share 2h ago 11.00 EST Preamble
 Boris Becker winning Wimbledon at 17 in 1985; Mike Tyson winning the world heavyweight boxing championship at 20 in 1986; Stephen Hendry winning the World Snooker Championships at 21 in 1990; Luke Littler winning the World Darts Championship in 2025; to which ludicrous list can now be added the name Kimi Antonelli, winner of the world driver championship at 20 in 2026.
 Of course the car has plenty to do with it, but finding the confidence and nous to beat around tracks men who’ve been driving them for years is a rare old effort – the next youngest to take the title, Sebastian Vettel in 2010, was 23 at the time. The question now, though, is whether Antonelli can go again, and again, and again, as the distractions away from the race multiply and the other freaks of nature who call this mad pursuit work, find holes in his game while closing some in their own.
 All of which makes today’s jaunt an important one: can the champ, starting second on the grid, lay down a marker for next season, advising his elders that there’ll be no letting up? Or will the piqued old stagers launch their fightback?
 Let’s find out!
 Lights out: 2pm local, 5pm GMT
